items.title: (Upcoming) What is the Best Root Beer?
items.summary: Today I’m proud to introduce Project Root. In the continued effort within the Clouty Skies Research Institute to determine the…
items.content_html:
Today I’m proud to introduce Project Root. In the continued effort within the Clouty Skies Research Institute to determine the best soda within a given flavor profile, we have moved on to root beer as our next study candidate. This phase evaluates 24 root beer products using the same standardized framework applied in Project Cream: an equal-weight, eight-metric scoring matrix with a maximum of 5 points per metric.

The evaluated metrics are Creaminess, Overall Taste, Smoothness, Design, Opening Experience, Ingredients, Price, and Availability.

The brands surveyed in Project Root, based strictly on the collected data, are A&W, A&W Sundae, Great Value, Signature Select, Sprecher’s, Jones, Poppi, Shasta, Nixie, Zevia, IBC, Teddy’s, Cove, Olipop, Elixir, River City, Virgil’s, Harvey’s, Abita, Daytrip, Live, Root Beer Wrath, Mug, and Barq’s.

Overall Rankings: This bar chart visualizes the total composite score for each root beer, calculated as the sum of all eight equally weighted evaluation metrics. Higher bars indicate stronger overall performance within the dataset.

Full Metric Breakdown: This table presents the complete scoring matrix for all evaluated products, showing individual metric scores and final totals. Values are displayed on a standardized 0–5 scale for direct comparison across brands.

Conclusion

Project Root demonstrates clear performance separation within the root beer category, with a small number of products consistently outperforming peers across the full eight-metric matrix while others show strength in isolated areas but weaker overall balance. These results reinforce the value of standardized, equal-weight evaluation when comparing consumer products within a single flavor profile.

For a full breakdown of the methodology, tasting process, and additional context behind the scores, watch the accompanying YouTube video. Future studies and expanded datasets will be published through the Clouty Skies Research Institute, with ongoing updates and new category analyses to follow.

Clouty Skies Research Institute

Project
Cream

 

An objective, unbiased dissertation on the performance, physics, and yumminess of the modern cream soda landscape.

Access Report
Historical Context

A Brief History of Cream

Before analyzing the modern landscape, one must understand the evolution of the vanilla-infused beverage.

 
1852

The First Patent

E.M. Howell patents the first written recipe for "cream soda." Unlike modern variants, this original concoction utilized water, sugar, tartaric acid, and egg whites to generate its signature creamy froth.

 
1886

The Gold Standard

Dr. Brown's introduces their iconic Cream Soda in New York. This sets the benchmark for the modern vanilla-heavy flavor profile that most traditional brands attempt to emulate today.

 
Mid-20th Century

The Pink Divergence

Regional variants emerge, most notably the "Pink" or "Red" cream sodas popularized in the Midwest and Canada. These rely heavily on artificial coloring and often lean closer to bubblegum or cotton candy flavor profiles.

 
Modern Era

The Functional Shift

The rise of prebiotic and functional sodas (Olipop, Poppi) introduces alternative sweeteners. The industry attempts to replicate the classic heavy mouthfeel without the caloric load, resulting in varying degrees of success.

The Methodology

We utilized an eight-point standardized matrix to evaluate the sensory and economic factors of 13 distinct brands.

Data Visualization

Ranking the Foam

Sugar is King

Superior sensory experiences (Creaminess, Taste) are overwhelmingly linked to traditional, caloric sweeteners like Honey or Cane Sugar.

The Functional Barrier

Zero-calorie alternatives consistently achieve high ingredient marks but fail dramatically in texture and flavor. Current technology cannot replicate the "Cream" profile.

Economy Paradox

Surprisingly, "Great Value" (Walmart) outperformed many mid-tier brands, proving that generic HFCS formulations often beat poorly executed "healthy" sodas.

items.content_html:
Official Publication

The Official
Wigga-Meter

A conceptual academic framework designed to quantify, categorize, and analyze the probability of encountering Wiggas in the wild.

Review Methodology
Framework Definition

Defining the Subject

Official Definition

"A usually young white person whose clothing, language, and mannerisms are regarded as imitative of those stereotypically associated with African-Americans : a white person who admires and seeks to emulate black culture"

Citation: “Wigger.” Merriam-Webster.com Dictionary, Merriam-Webster, https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/wigger. Accessed 4 Jun. 2026.

CSRI's Working Definition

A suburban white individual who adopts the aesthetic of urban rap culture, often identifying with cities like the Bronx or Atlanta based solely on lyrical exposure.

It is critical to differentiate the process from the result. To achieve Wiggerdom, one must undergo the arduous journey of Wiggermaxing. This process requires years of practice, yelling at your girlfriend, extensive auditory exposure, drug abuse, and more yelling. Wiggerdom is the final, enlightened end state of this developmental process.

The Four Variables

  • NWAL: Natural Appearance Likelihood in public spaces.
  • WEC: Wage/Employment Correlation probability.
  • BSA: Bluetooth Speaker Allowance (public broadcast tolerance).
  • FFP: Free Food/Drink Probability via networking.

Historical Context & Media Analysis

The "First" Encounter & Comedic Observation

Comedian Theodor Capitani von Kurnatowski III ( Theo Von ) famously describes what he presumes was "The First Wigger." Alongside his account, Bill Burr provides a quintessential analysis of how a Wigger may appear to the general population.

Historical Accounts & Early Media

The phenomenon began drawing serious media attention in the early 1990s. The Washington Post's 1993 broadcast stands as one of the earliest mainstream examples documenting the cultural shift, supported by archival footage from Hezakya Newz & Films from 1999.

Hallmarks of Wigger Awareness

Published on August 27, 2006, nearly 20 years ago, this early days YouTube clip provides a more in-depth look at authentic mannerisms at the absolute height of the movement.

The Modern State of Wiggerdom

Today, Wigger is almost a state of mind. It is now considered "cool" in many circles to embody the persona, although modern practitioners are often more "Wigga's" merely emulating the Old Guard Wiggers of the 1990s and 2000s rather than organically developing the traits.

The aesthetic has even cross-pollinated into extreme music. There is now an entire subgenre of Deathcore called Wigger Slam; a trashier aesthetic built directly upon the heavy, rhythmic breakdowns of Slam Metal.

items.content_html:
About the Clouty Skies Research Institute

The Clouty Skies Research Institute is a data-driven platform dedicated to publishing structured, transparent research on consumer products and other areas of interest. We specialize in exploring the cultural and consumer intersections that mainstream academics often overlook. While traditional institutions focus on theoretical abstractions, CSRI addresses interesting and engaging topics for everyday people, providing tangible data they can reference in their daily lives.

Built to complement the work we do in videos and social media, the Institute website provides a centralized place to explore full breakdowns, standardized metrics, and datasets derived from systematic evaluation projects. Our methodology prioritizes "Real-World Utility," ensuring that every data point serves a practical purpose for our audience.

Current Research Pillars

  • Project Cream: A comprehensive sensory and market analysis where multiple cream soda brands were scored using consistent, multi-variable criteria to determine peak consumer value.

  • The Wigga-Meter: An exploratory sociological framework designed to quantify encounter probabilities within specific environments. This project utilizes our proprietary WiggerFactor metrics to provide a standardized scale for demographic and environmental analysis.

Our Goal

The site is organized to make research accessible and verifiable, with sections for posts, projects, data, and background on our methodology. Our goal is to offer a resource where viewers and readers can dive deeper into the data behind the findings, follow ongoing research efforts, and engage with the process behind each project. By bridging the gap between rigorous data analysis and public engagement, we provide a new standard for independent research.
